81575e268768.title: Senior Navigation Engineer
81575e268768.description: As a Senior Navigation Engineer at Impulse Space, you will own the state estimation and orbit determination systems that let our vehicles know where they are and where they're going, across all phases of development and operation, while working closely with a fast-paced, agile team. You will design, implement, and validate the navigation filters and sensor-fusion techniques that fly our spacecraft and orbital transfer vehicles in LEO, GEO, and cislunar space, as well as perform astrodynamic analyses required for mission success. Design, develop, and tune navigation and estimation algorithms (EKF/UKF, batch/sequential estimators) for spacecraft and high-ΔV orbital transfer vehicles. Perform spacecraft navigation analyses: orbit determination, attitude determination, astrodynamic trajectories, covariance analysis, and navigation error budgets. Develop and validate sensor models and measurement models (IMU, GNSS/GPS, star tracker, optical/relative navigation, radiometric). Implement navigation algorithms in flight code (C++) and support SIL/HIL integration and test. Run Monte Carlo analysis to characterize navigation performance under dispersed and off-nominal conditions. Generate navigation verification data across Impulse's suite of missions. Support navigation operations: real-time OD, console support, and anomaly response during critical mission phases. Communicate navigation design needs, intent, performance, trades, and risk to the broader engineering team.

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. 96bfd8b4dd52.title: Member of Technical Staff, Full-Stack AI Engineer/Researcher (Staff+ Level)
96bfd8b4dd52.description: THE MISSION More than 95% of drugs that pass animal testing fail in human trials. A single new drug takes about $2.6 billion and 12.5 years to develop, and most of that effort goes to candidates that were never going to work in people. AI was supposed to change this. But most AI for drug discovery is still trained on the same inputs that got us here: animal data, irreproducible papers, and cell lines that don’t respond like living tissue. A model can only learn the biology it’s shown, and no amount of scale or compute fixes bad data. What’s missing is data on how living human tissue responds to a drug, across the range of people who will actually take it. That data barely exists, because there has been no way to generate it at scale without putting patients at risk. Parallel Bio grows it. Our expert biologists build living human immune systems, called immune organoids, from a proprietary biobank spanning ages, sexes, ancestries and disease states. That means we can ask how a drug behaves in an older patient, a specific ancestry or an autoimmune background, not just in an average donor. We've already modeled immunotoxicology, immunogen stimulation and two autoimmune diseases, with more on the way. Our founders are world experts in scalable organoids. Robert is a Stanford-trained immunologist. Juliana trained in the lab that invented the first organoid and later automated them at System1 Biosciences. We run these experiments in an AI-driven robotic lab, and every experiment makes our world model smarter, which in turn chooses better experiments. We build every layer ourselves: the biology, the robotics, the data infrastructure, and the model that orchestrates it all. The whole lab is callable over API and MCP, so AI agents can design and run real biological experiments, within safety limits we set. For biologists, that means asking questions at a scale and pace no bench can match. For engineers, it means building AI that learns from real human biology instead of the literature. It's already working. Our platform is 87% concordant with clinical outcomes, compared with roughly 3% translational success for animal models. Five Fortune 500 companies use it to test drugs, and our data has informed a Phase 1 trial. We've raised ~$30M from AIX Ventures, Marc Benioff, Jeff Dean and Y Combinator. With the FDA Modernization Act 3.0 and the FDA's March 2026 validation framework, regulation is moving our way. The opportunity is generational. We're building the first scaled engine for real human biological data, and using it to know which drugs will work in people before they ever reach a trial. YOUR SKILLS Must be able to operate across the entire AI stack: evals, agentic harnesses, and models Parallel Bio is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, religion, disability, or sexual orientation.

7028f5b6b0e1.title: Equipment Engineer
7028f5b6b0e1.description:
About Neuralink:

We are creating devices that enable a bi-directional interface with the brain. These devices allow us to restore movement to the paralyzed, restore sight to the blind, and revolutionize how humans interact with their digital world.

Team Description: 

Operating out of our Fremont cleanroom facility, the Microfabrication group fabricates thin-film polymer electrode arrays (termed "threads") integral to Neuralink implants. Our team executes the complete internal process flow, spanning photolithography, thin-film deposition, etching, polyimide processing, electroplating, metrology, and final release. Collaborating closely with process engineering, quality, and implant assembly teams, we support the ramp from initial development runs to clinical and eventually commercial manufacturing scale. The equipment engineering group directly maintains total tool availability, capability, and qualification across the cleanroom to ensure continuous high-yield array output and rapid iteration.

Job Description and Responsibilities:

  • Maintain continuous operational readiness and uptime for microfabrication equipment, including photolithography steppers, PVD systems, PECVD, plasma etchers, track coaters, electroplating units, and metrology tools.
  • Perform root-cause diagnostics and repairs across electrical, mechanical, vacuum, pneumatic, RF, and control systems, implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrent failures.
  • Establish and execute preventive maintenance protocols, covering chamber cleans, component replacements, seasoning routines, and post-maintenance hardware requalifications.
  • Lead installation, facility integration, qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ), and formal release of new processing equipment, as well as deinstallations or equipment relocations.
  • Monitor key operational metrics such as MTBF, MTTR, tool availability, and SPC data to drive preventive maintenance strategies and inventory planning.
  • Oversee critical spare parts inventory, consumables, vendor service agreements, and technical interface with original equipment manufacturers.
  • Partner with process engineering to resolve yield excursions, optimize tool matching, and execute hardware upgrades to support process development.
  • Generate and maintain SOPs, PM specifications, and equipment logs in compliance with medical device quality standards and change control requirements.
  • Instruct cleanroom technicians and operating staff on proper tool safety protocols, operation, and initial fault diagnosis.
  • Collaborate with facilities management to support sub-fab infrastructure, including high-purity process gases, house vacuum, DI water, and exhaust systems.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree

00a96acc7814.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Robotics
00a96acc7814.description:
Build the Path Forward

At Path Robotics, we’re building the future of embodied intelligence. Our AI-driven systems enable robots to adapt, learn, and perform in the real world closing the skilled labor gap and transforming industries. We go beyond traditional methods, combining perception, reasoning, and control to deliver field-ready AI that is risk-aware, reliable, and continuously improving through real-world use.

Big, hard problems are our everyday work, and our team of intelligent, humble, and driven people make the impossible possible together.

We're seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to join our Robotics team. You'll use machine learning to improve how our robots plan, scan, and act. You'll frame real robot problems as well-defined ML problems, train models on data that a fleet of production robotic cells generates every day, and ship them into a production stack where they work alongside classical planning and perception. Your models run on live robots doing real work for customers.

What You'll Do

  • Frame open-ended problems in planning, scanning, and robot behavior as well-defined ML problems.
  • Train models that work with classical methods, such as initial guesses and learned costs for trajectory optimization, plan quality and feasibility predictors, and learned collision models.
  • Develop viewpoint planning policies that choose where and how to scan, and predict scan quality before the robot commits.
  • Apply imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and generative models such as diffusion and flow matching where they outperform classical baselines.
  • Build production ML pipelines: datasets from fleet logs and simulation, training, and metrics.
  • Evaluate models in the loop, with offline metrics that predict gains on the robot, failure-mode analysis, and calibrated confidence that determines when the system falls back to classical methods.
  • Own your models end to end, from prototype to deployment on live robotic cells, with low-latency inference and monitoring.

Who You Are

  • An MS or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, or a related field.
  • 4+ years of applied machine learning for robotics or autonomy, in research or industry.
  • Fluent in Python with PyTorch or JAX, and experienced training, evaluating, and deploying deep learning models.
  • Strong foundations in linear algebra, 3D geometry, kinematics, and optimization.
  • You've run your methods on real robot hardware.
  • You explain model results and their limits clearly, so planning, perception, and field teams know when to trust them.

Preferred

  • C++, and experience deploying models into a C++ or ROS 2 production stack.
  • Motion planning, trajectory optimization, or collision che

What you'll do Take ownership of research problems end-to-end: literature review, hypothesis, prototype, empirical validation, shadow-mode evaluation, and handoff to production. Contribute to invention disclosures when your work produces novel, patentable mechanisms.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT RAMP LABS Ramp Labs is Ramp's AI research and engineering group. We post-train models on finance work, build the environments and evals they learn from, and ship them into the products 85,000+ companies use to move money. ABOUT THE ROLE Most agent work today is one agent, one trace, and a person reads the result. We're building systems where that stops working: thousands of agents fanned out over a large search space, each returning partial results, with an orchestrator that turns all of it into something useful: hundreds of merged PRs, a dataset, the input to another system, or something nobody has built yet. You'll design and run those systems: how work gets split, how agents coordinate, how results get deduplicated, verified and ranked, and what it all costs. The problems are general (agent swarms, agentic map-reduce, long-running fan-out workflows) and you'll own them from prototype to production. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Decide how the work gets done: how to break a problem down, what each agent sees, how many agents to run, and which model handles which step - Squeeze accuracy out of the models: context design, self-verification, voting and consensus across agents, and knowing when more agents stop helping - Measure quality without reading every trace: sampling, automated verification, and precision and recall on the final output - Drive down cost and latency per useful result: model routing, caching, early stopping, and smaller or fine-tuned models where they hold up - Turn one-off experiments into reusable workflows on our existing orchestration stack - Evaluate new models, inference setups and training approaches, and bring in what works WHAT YOU NEED - Experience building applied AI systems and LLM applications that shipped - Hands-on experience with multi-agent or high-fan-out LLM workloads: parallel agents, map-reduce over models, large batch inference - Strong engineering in Python; you build concurrent, distributed systems that hold up in production - Judgment about output: you decide what the end result should look

Our team builds the vehicle dynamics models that help show Torc’s autonomous trucks are safe. We develop high-fidelity simulations of how a Class 8 tractor-trailer brakes, steers, and handles load. Those models feed safety analysis, scenario simulation, and the safety case across Torc.

As a Senior Systems Engineer – Vehicle Dynamics, you’ll lead this work in-house. You’ll own and grow our Simulink-based vehicle dynamics tools, correlate them against real-world test data, and work with safety, controls, path planning, and systems teams to turn the results into design decisions for our autonomous truck platform.

What You’ll Do:

  • Develop and maintain vehicle dynamics models for Class 8 tractor-trailers that capture handling, stability, braking, ride, and load transfer behavior across a range of operating conditions and vehicle configurations.
  • Build and refine Simulink models of combination-vehicle dynamics, working closely with suspension, steering, tire, and braking subsystem models to improve vehicle performance predictions.
  • Analyze vehicle test data from the proving ground, on-road testing, and simulation to characterize dynamic behavior, validate models against real-world performance, and support root-cause investigations of handling, stability, and ride issues.
  • Support correlation between simulation models and physical test data to improve model fidelity and predictive accuracy.
  • Write and maintain MATLAB scripts that automate simulation setup, run vehicle dynamics test scenarios, and post-process simulation and test data.
  • Collaborate with systems, safety, controls, path planning, and operations teams to apply vehicle dynamics analysis to design decisions for our vehicle platforms.
  • Contribute to new simulation tools, automation scripts, and analysis workflows, incorporating AI-assisted tools and techniques where applicable to improve team efficiency.
  • Document modeling assumptions, scripts, and analysis methods, and analyze their risks, to build confidence in their use and support knowledge sharing and consistency across vehicle dynamics work.

What You Need to Succeed:

  • Hands-on experience simulating articulated vehicle dynamics.
  • Deep, hands-on experience with MATLAB and Simulink for vehicle dynamics modeling and analysis.
  • Experience evaluating and qualifying tools to establish confidence for use in safety-critical systems.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across cross-functional engineering teams.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

BACKEND SOFTWARE ENGINEER, GNC (STARLINK)

At SpaceX, we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.

As a software engineer working in Starlink’s Space Safety team, you will use your distributed systems knowledge to build mission-critical systems that keep low-earth orbit safe. With over 100 launches in 2025 and over 10,000 satellites on orbit, Starlink requires a high degree of automation to fly safely. You’ll work on collision avoidance, space situational awareness, and orbit determination tools for our constellation, making sure can avoid debris and other spacecraft—from pre-launch through deorbit.

Our software engineers are responsible for the complete lifecycle of the software they create, including development, testing, and support. We expect our engineers to close the feedback loop between software design and real-world performance. In this role, your software will have a meaningful and measurable impact on the world.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop highly reliable and available software systems for managing thousands of satellites in low-earth orbit.
  • Participate in architecture, design, and code reviews.
  • Develop prototypes to prove out key design concepts and quantify technical constraints.
  • Develop tools for software development and deployment, data analysis and visualization, and test execution across multiple environments, including virtualized hardware environments, real hardware-in-the-loop simulations, and on-orbit testing.
  • Deploy reliable software, test execution, and data analysis as part of a continuous integration and release system.

  • Bachelors degree in STEM & 1+ year of industry and/or internship experience; OR 2+ years of professional software development experience in lieu of a STEM degree.
  • Professional experience writing code in C++, Python, Golang, or similar.

eca6f4e23bc2.description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.

This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.

This role supports Okta's U.S. federal environments and requires U.S. federal eligibility, including U.S. citizenship.

The Team

Okta Workflows is a no-code automation platform that lets IT and security teams automate identity processes at scale: onboarding and offboarding, access requests, event-driven responses to security signals, and integrations across hundreds of SaaS applications. Every one of those automations ultimately runs on a single execution engine, and that is where this team lives.

The Opportunity

The Engine Kernel team owns the runtime that executes every Okta Workflow. Our engine treats a workflow the way an operating system treats a process: it schedules, pauses, resumes, and coordinates executions across a high-throughput, multi-region distributed system. The engine is written in Rust and runs on Kubernetes.

We are accountable for the reliability, scale, performance, and cost of the core workflow lifecycle, and we hold a very high bar for availability because our customers' identity automation depends on it.

Some of the problems you would work on:

  • Durable execution: evolving how the engine persists and recovers workflow state so long-running automations are resilient by design.
  • Smarter scheduling: reducing the cost of durability so the engine can checkpoint work cheaply and keep latency low and predictable.

TITLE: Senior Software Engineer

REPORTING TO: CTO

LOCATION: Marina del Rey, CA – OR – Williamsburg, NY (onsite M - F)

Who Is Flip?

Flip builds AI voice agents that handle millions of real customer conversations for some of the biggest brands, healthcare providers, and transportation companies in the world. When you call a company and the AI actually solves your problem — tracks the order, processes the return, refills the prescription — that’s us.

We’re a low-ego team. We don’t need the limelight or the stardom — we care about solving really hard problems, fast. And here’s the part worth stopping on: outside the frontier labs, almost nobody is running AI in production at this scale. We are — millions and millions of live phone calls, at a ratio of roughly one engineer for every million calls. We deploy to production three times a day. Very few teams our size serve this volume, and the reason is simple: we hold a very high bar for development.

How we think

From day one, we’ve operated on first principles, and the first principle is the customer. If you have strong conviction that something delivers real business value for your customer, it shouldn’t die in red tape or committee. You ship it — fast and often — because the customer is what actually matters. That’s why there’s a direct line from your keyboard to production here. We didn’t remove the committee to move fast for its own sake; we removed it because conviction plus customer obsession doesn’t need a permission slip.

We reward big swings. Our founders are very forward about this: you’ll test in production, and you’ll always be encouraged to take a swing — whether it lands or not. Missing on a big swing is fine. Not swinging is what gets called out.

Agentic development has changed the way we work — we’re not shy about that. What it hasn’t changed is the necessity of experience, especially at the production level. You can ship faster than ever now; that doesn’t negate experience. Speed without judgment is how you break things millions of people depend on. That’s why we hire senior engineers: builders whose experience makes the new speed safe.

Our view is simple: let builders build. We care a lot less about stack experience or corporate pedigree than most companies — and a lot more about whether you’ve looked past the noise and want to build product you’re genuinely proud of. Tools change monthly now. The instinct to build doesn’t.

We keep the team lean on purpose — a high bar, real support, real resources — because that’s where builders truly express themselves. The most common thing we hear from engineers after joining Flip is some version of “I could never have done this at my last company”.

Deep industry expertise matched with ruthless execution creates wonder

Lila Sciences is seeking a highly experienced, creative, and talented Machine Learning Researcher (Open-Endedness) to join our team.

May Mobility is transforming cities through autonomous technology to create a safer, greener, more accessible world. Based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, May develops and deploys autonomous vehicles (AVs) powered by our innovative Multi-Policy Decision Making (MPDM) technology that literally reimagines the way AVs think.

Our vehicles do more than just drive themselves - they provide value to communities, bridge public transit gaps and move people where they need to go safely, easily and with a lot more fun. We’re building the world’s best autonomy system to reimagine transit by minimizing congestion, expanding access and encouraging better land use in order to foster more green, vibrant and livable spaces. Since our founding in 2017, we’ve given more than 500,000 autonomous rides to real people around the globe. And we’re just getting started. We’re hiring people who share our passion for building the future, today, solving real-world problems and seeing the impact of their work. Join us.

Job Summary

This Manager will be responsible for leading the vision, strategy, and technical roadmap for ML Engineering functions at May Mobility.  This position plays a key role in advancing May’s core autonomy software stack, applying Autonomy Models to ML challenges across the organization, and charting the path for the supporting ML Platform and Operations infrastructure to maintain velocity.

This position reports to the Director of Autonomy Modeling and is responsible for providing world class leadership to our Autonomy Engineering, Software and Data Engineers, in order to propel their professional success as they develop industry-leading technology advancements.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Oversee day-to-day development, training, evaluation and deployment of ML models across edge and cloud/on-prem targets.
  • Maintain technical roadmaps for accelerating ML performance and operations across the organization
  • Collaborate with other Autonomy teams, Safety teams, and Advanced Engineering teams to deploy robust, generalizable models for autonomous vehicles
  • Track and trend the performance and development of ML models across the organization 
  • Support site/field integration, performance evaluation, system verification, and product launch/deployment in US and global sites
  • Support and calibrate the performance of 5+ Engineers across a wide range of ML-related specialties

b4305c9d0716.title: Founding Clinical Engineer, US
b4305c9d0716.description: I quit medicine because I kept watching patients die needlessly, for avoidable reasons. In almost every case, the medical knowledge and clinicians were there. It was the system that failed: the way information moved, decisions got routed, and fragmented teams and data turned solvable problems into tragedy. I started Anima to change that. Our mission is to maximise human wellbeing, delivered through personalised medicine. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes. This learning engine is the beating heart of Anima. We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~50 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions. Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them. If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives. -- Shun WHAT THIS ROLE IS You'll be the founding engineering hire for our US expansion. - Working with our GTM lead, you'll travel the country speaking to prospective customers, understanding their pain and building Anima’s first product in the USA. - You'll own the US product end to end, and be accountable for everything from architecting the solution to ensuring compliance with our customers’ and federal safety requirements. - You'll work on a well-established product stack that's already highly scalable, cost effective, secure and performant, and already supports primary care (GP) workflows for >20% of patients in the UK. - You'll be supported by our incredibly smart team in NAMR, the UK and APAC. Like Michael, who built a working CPU from logic gates at age 16 and co-founded YC-backed Embark Trucks, the first self-driving vehicle on Canadian roads; or Souradip, who built an acoustic fall detector using on-device deep learning; he's also an MB/PhD from Cambridge who's published in top medical journals. - You'll do whatever is needed to solve the problem. We're tech-agnostic and collectively choose the best tools for the job. We're constantly looking to maximise our productivity and minimise what we call "discounted dev time cost" for shipping features. You'll report to Jake, our US go-to-market lead, and work alongside our product and engineering team in London. Because you'll work directly with US patient data, this role is based in the US. WHO YOU ARE You’re literate in the US healthcare system. - Ideally you trained in medicine and worked as a clinician before moving into engineering. - If not, you've built real products inside US healthcare and are comfortable having detailed conversations with healthcare stakeholders to deeply understand their pains. - You understand the US healthcare system very well, and you're confident dealing with staff in healthcare systems

99554449978a.title: Data Center Engineer - Critical Faciliites
99554449978a.description:
Verisign helps enable the security, stability, and resiliency of the internet. We are a trusted provider of internet infrastructure services for the networked world and deliver unmatched performance in domain name system (DNS) services. 

We are a mission focused, values driven company where each individual can contribute to building a stronger, more secure internet.  We offer a dynamic and flexible work environment with competitive benefits and the ability to grow your career.

We are seeking a Senior Critical Facilities Engineer (Data Center Operations) to serve as a technical resource and leader within the Global Data Center Operations Team. This onsite role at our Ashburn Data Center will play a crucial role in the day-to-day operations & capacity planning of mission critical systems. 

The ideal candidate will have technical and program management expertise in the maintenance and operation of electrical, mechanical, and fire life safety data center systems as well as applicable base building support systems.  You will support the Director – Data Center & Facilities Operations as a technical lead.  While this is an individual contributor role, you must be able to direct and inspire highly skilled engineers, deliver on project timelines and be the technical point of contact for on-call escalations.  Clear and concise written and verbal communication skills along with experience developing Standard Operating Procedures, Emergency Operating Procedures and Method of Procedures utilizing technical writing standards are a must.

Mechanical responsibilities include chilled water systems and components, HVAC systems such as roof top units, CRAC/CRAH units, and humidification systems.  Electrical responsibilities will include electrical/critical power distribution from the Utility/Generator main switchgear through the UPS, STS, and PDU system to the power on the data center floor.  Fire Life Safety responsibilities will include wet sprinkler systems, pre-action sprinkler systems, clean agent fire suppression systems and fire alarm systems as well as their associated detection devices.

The candidate will:

  • operate independently with limited direct management
  • act as an escalation point for all facilities-related issues within the data center, escalating to the Director – Data Center & Facilities Operations as needed
  • ensure all electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety equipment supporting the data centers are operating at peak efficiency and are highly available
  • identify Single Points of Failures (SPoF) and End of Life (EOL) equipment within existing design/architecture and drive prioritization/remediation efforts within the facility
  • drive preventative maintenance best practices and oversight using Method of Procedures (MOP) and Emergency Operating Procedures (EOP) for the facility

f98703c88647.description: Location: Pittsburgh, PA Why Confluence? At Confluence, we’ve always been driven by a commitment to innovation, precision, and partnership in the investment data space. Our global footprint now spans multiple countries, giving our employees the opportunity to get exposure to other countries and cultures. And it stands to reason that none of this would have been possible without the hundreds of hard-working employees who work at Confluence. The Data Team is building the next-generation data platform — a multi-tenant platform that will become the shared data layer behind our applications. At the heart of that platform is a Python data API built on a layered router → service → repository architecture, containerized with Docker and deployed entirely through infrastructure-as-code. Today the platform is SQL Server-heavy, and part of this role is migrating business and data logic out of legacy stored procedures into testable Python — parameterized SQL for retrieval, pandas for computation and reshaping. As we evolve, we intend to grow well beyond a single database — incorporating additional and modern data sources (for example, Snowflake, which the API's SQLAlchemy-based connection registry is already designed to add) and the patterns needed to serve them through a unified API. This is a foundational, shaping role: you will help define the architecture and direction of that next-generation platform, not just maintain what exists. We are seeking a Software Engineer with a strong data-engineering focus to join the Data Team. The role is primarily focused on the data API, but it is a team role rather than a single-service one — you will work across the data platform as it grows. This is backend- and data-centric work: you will spend more time on data correctness, performance, and the movement and reconciliation of large datasets across heterogeneous sources than on any single framework or UI library. We value depth in the core technologies and engineering fundamentals over expertise in any specific component, and we expect enough Azure and DevOps capability to deploy and operate what you build.

The Trade Desk is a global technology company and the world’s leading independent platform for digital advertising, with over 3,000 employees across more than 30 offices. When you work here, your impact is worldwide. We welcome diverse perspectives, encourage curiosity, and build teams that learn from one another. If you’re driven to solve meaningful challenges, we’d love to meet you.

About the role 

Every campaign on our platform has a budget and a flight, and our pacing system decides in real time how to spend it against 20M queries per second. It has to bid the right amount on every impression, at the right rate, so advertisers spend their budget in full and get the most value from it. 

Changing a system like that safely is its own engineering problem. An ordinary A/B traffic split breaks down here, because both arms draw on the same campaign budget and one arm's spend distorts the other. We solve this with budget split experiments: each arm gets its own share of the budget, its own pacing calculation and its own spend tracking, all inside one live campaign. This is now how we gain confidence in any change to bidding behavior. 

We are looking for a senior engineer to work across both areas: the pacing engine itself, and the experimentation infrastructure that proves changes to it. You will build in the services that compute pacing instructions and apply them at bid time. You will also extend the experiment framework so teams across the company can launch a trustworthy experiment in hours instead of weeks.

We also help product teams measure authentic usage so that abuse doesn’t distort decisions about how our products are growing. Integrity Data Science helps teams decide where to intervene and whether those interventions work. A payment control can prevent fraud while blocking legitimate purchases. A product launch can make it easier for customers to get started while creating new opportunities for abuse. We measure both sides of those decisions. ABOUT THE ROLE As a Senior/Staff Software Engineer on Suno’s new Bots & Fraud team, you’ll design and build the backend systems behind our defenses against abuse, fraud, and bots. You’ll build real-time services that turn request telemetry, behavioral signals, and device and app attestation into enforcement, such as rate limits, challenges, and account actions, across every layer from the edge to product services. The team is new and pulls together work from across the company, so you’ll help shape what we build and how we build it. You’ll report to the Bots & Fraud Engineering Manager. WHAT YOU'LL NEED MUST-HAVES - 5+ years of software engineering experience - 3+ years of backend development on distributed systems - 2+ years of experience in trust and safety, anti-abuse, or fraud prevention - Experience leading projects from design through launch and mentoring other engineers NICE-T

By offering greater choice over how and when payments are made and allowing eligible on time payments to help build a positive credit history, Flex puts households back in control of their cash flow.

That work brings together people with different perspectives who challenge the status quo and take ownership of solving difficult problems. For you, that means doing the best work of your career next to people who make you better, and together bringing ideas to life that make a real impact for the people we serve.

About the Role

Flex is seeking a Legal Engineer to design, build, and maintain the AI-enabled tooling that powers our Legal team. Our legal organization is already on the bleeding edge of AI adoption, and this role exists to push that further: turning commercial and corporate legal work into automated, scalable workflows, and equipping our product and regulatory advisory colleagues with tools that let them advise at the speed of the business. By owning legal automation end to end, you will help Legal stay lean, keep pace with the business, and ensure risk is managed by design rather than by headcount.

This is a builder role with a product mindset. You will sit at the intersection of law, operations, and technology: spotting where work can be automated, scoping and prioritizing solutions like a product manager, building them yourself, and measuring whether they work.

What You Will Do

  • Own Legal’s AI use-case roadmap: identify, scope, and prioritize automation opportunities across commercial, corporate, and product/regulatory advisory work, and make build-versus-buy recommendations backed by a clear business case.
  • Design, build, and maintain AI-enabled tools and workflows (custom agents, prompt templates, review checklists, intake pipelines, and system integrations) that automate contract review, drafting, and corporate housekeeping.
  • Connect legal tooling to the systems the business already runs on (e.g., Ironclad, Salesforce, Snowflake, Superblocks) so data flows end to end and the business can self-serve through intake paths, FAQ tooling, and dashboards.
  • Partner with product and regulatory counsel to build tools that help them advise on product launches, marketing, and regulatory change quickly and consistently.
  • Build risk management into every workflow: define where AI output requires attorney review or escalation, and ensure AI usage aligns with Flex’s AI-usage policy and data-classification rules.

0bdc8da17d4c.description:
Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads.

Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter!

If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders.

Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light!

As a Design Verification Engineer at Lightmatter, you will find yourself at the heart of a dynamic, interdisciplinary team. Your role will involve close collaboration with our digital design experts, using UVM testbench techniques to rigorously verify their designs. Your responsibilities will include working alongside photonic and analog designers, gaining a deep understanding of their innovative designs, and applying Real Number Modeling (RNM) and AMS verification methods. This critical function ensures the integrity of their work. We are hiring at multiple levels. 

Your interaction with the Architecture team will be crucial in comprehending system requirements and spearheading performance verification. This role offers a unique platform to enhance your skills across a spectrum of areas including UVM, AMS modeling, mixed-signal verification, post-silicon validation formal verification, emulation, and both performance modeling and verification.

Responsibilities

  • Define and enhance the DV methodologies required for integrated digital, analog, and photonic devices with a strong emphasis on emulation for design verification.
  • Create and execute test plans to ensure high-quality tapeouts that meet functional and performance goals, while leveraging emulation where appropriate.
  • Collaborate with architects, DV engineers, digital designers, and analog/photonics designers to define validation flows.
  • Create reusable and scalable test bench components that enable efficient and effective verification.
  • Close coverage and finish all DV signoff requirements, with a focus on leveraging mixed signal simulations to achieve high coverage metrics
  • Work on block level and full chip design verification.
  • Integrate analog design IPs from vendors and internal teams and develop verification environments for simulation and emulation.
  • Work with analog design engineers to create behavioral models for analog designs and with digital design engineers to integrate models/testcase/checkers into upper levels

The Scout brand is all about respect. This is a place where your fingerprints are found on metal – where what you design gets built, driven, and remembered. e421a39bc2ae.title: Senior, Vehicle Integration Engineer
e421a39bc2ae.description:
Kodiak AI, Inc. (Nasdaq: KDK), founded in 2018, is a leader in Physical AI, developing driverless technology that powers machines that move. Its Kodiak Driver is a vehicle-agnostic autonomous driving system that combines AI-powered software with modular hardware. Today it operates in long-haul trucking, industrial trucking, and defense. In 2024, Kodiak launched commercial Driver-as-a-Service operations with no one in the cab, and plans to launch driverless long-haul service between Dallas and Houston by the end of 2026.

Kodiak has partnered with many of the biggest names in freight, including Bosch for scaled hardware production, AWS, and leading customers including Atlas Energy Solutions, IKEA, Bridgestone, Werner Enterprises, C.R. England, Roehl Transport, and General Dynamics Land Systems.

We are looking for a Senior Vehicle Integration Engineer with deep experience in new platform development and system-level integration. This role is at the forefront of bringing next-generation autonomous vehicle platforms to life — from early-stage concept through integration, validation, and deployment. You will work closely with hardware, systems, and manufacturing teams to drive new platform development, with a focus on integration quality, test rigor, and technical execution.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead system-level integration of sensors, compute, actuation, and vehicle systems for new platform development programs
  • Drive the full integration lifecycle: architecture definition, build planning, bring-up, validation, and sign-off
  • Develop and execute structured test plans to validate new platform functionality, performance, and reliability
  • Coordinate and lead cross-functional build and integration events with Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, and Systems teams
  • Provide Design-For-Manufacturing and Design-For-Test feedback to ensure new platforms are built for quality and scale
  • Develop and maintain comprehensive platform documentation including drawings, schematics, BOMs, build instructions, and test reports
  • Identify, triage, and resolve integration issues through systematic debugging and root cause analysis
  • Partner with systems and hardware engineering teams to define integration requirements and acceptance criteria for new platforms

4fdf84e83d80.description:
About the Company

Cartesian is building spatial intelligence for indoor environments to drive operational efficiency.

We’re tackling one of the biggest challenges in the $35T global retail industry: in-store inventory visibility. Our platform delivers accurate indoor positioning and actionable product location insights, helping retailers streamline operations, optimize workflows, and reduce inefficiencies. By fusing wireless signals and mobile computer vision, we provide a uniquely scalable and infrastructure-free solution already deployed by international fashion brands.

Founded by an MIT engineering professor and alum behind the award-winning, patented core technologies, Cartesian spun out in 2023. Originally backed by the prestigious SBIR Award from the US National Science Foundation, we've bootstrapped to a live product that's now deployed in over a dozen countries and have been aggressively scaling in the market.

About the Role

We’re looking for a highly motivated, product-oriented Machine Learning Scientist to join our core R&D team at a pivotal moment in our growth. You'll have a direct impact on key positioning algorithms & models, take ownership of new features, and help shape the technical roadmap of a category-defining product. We move fast, care deeply about quality, and value people who take initiative and crave real-world impact. 

You’ll be joining us in-person in the heart of Kendall Square, Cambridge, next to MIT and the Charles River.

 

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and deploy ML models for indoor positioning and perception.

  • Optimize model architectures for performance and efficiency.

  • Develop tools and datasets to benchmark performance in the real world and at scale.

  • Translate research into production pipelines.

  • Collaborate with engineering and product to ship features to enterprise customers.

     

Qualifications

  • PhD in computer science, electrical engineering, or related field.

  • Deep understanding and hands-on experience in machine learning models for time-series data, including both transformer-based architectures and probabilistic models (e.g., state estimation). 

  • Publications in top-tier ML, vision, or systems venues (e.g., ACL, NeurIPS, CVPR, ECCV, ICCV, MobiCom, MobiSys, MLSys, ICASSP, ICML, ICRL, ICRA, IROS).

  • Ability to write high-quality production code. 

  • Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate across disciplines. 

  • Thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments and take pride in producing high-quality work.

What is Coast

Coast is re-imagining the trillion-dollar U.S. B2B card payments infrastructure, with a focus on the country’s 500,000 commercial fleets, 40 million commercial vehicles, and many millions of commercial drivers. The incumbent technologies that cater to these customers are decades old, and businesses with fleets increasingly demand modern digital experiences and transparent financial services products. Coast’s mission is to deliver this at a transformational scale, beginning with the Coast Fleet and Fuel Card built on a cutting-edge spend management platform.

About the Role

At Coast, Platform builds the shared foundations every product team relies on: our standards, infrastructure, and developer tooling. We want it to support our product and engineering organization and multiply impact and expertise, so people spend their time on what makes their work special. The right platform lets every team move faster with control, because the safe way is also the easiest way. We’re hiring a Engineer, reporting to our Head of Platform, to build the paved paths that make that possible.

You may have done this work as a DevOps, SRE, Infrastructure, or AI Platform engineer. Whatever it’s called, at its core it’s a software engineering job. You’ll write the code and build the tools our teams ship on, from the first commit to production, and everything that keeps it secure, resilient, observable, and fast. The goal is self-service, with paved paths that strike the right balance between freedom and responsibility, so teams move fast without waiting on anyone.

AI is changing how software gets built, and parts of this work are new. The problems underneath are not: shipping safely, keeping systems reliable, and helping teams move faster are things engineers have worked on for decades. We want someone who builds on that history instead of starting over with every new tool. In financial services, regulations, customer expectations, and industry standards are moving too. You’ll keep Coast on the cutting edge and move our platform toward the next best practice that meets our needs. Platform partners across the company, including AI Operations, Risk, Data Analytics, IT, and RevOps, and you’ll make sure every improvement, wherever it comes from, benefits everyone.

What You’ll Do

  • Build the Paved Paths
    • Build self-service paths from commit to production: fast builds, end-to-end testing, preview environments, and release and rollback automation
    • Keep our infrastructure secure, resilient, and observable, with infrastructure as code on AWS, Zero Trust networking, multi-region resiliency, and SLOs teams can rely on
    • Listen to what teams across Coast ask for, solve the problems behind those asks, and make everyone more efficient
    • Hold a high bar for quality in what you build, as that will compound on ev

97028d98de0d.title: Senior Backend Engineer
97028d98de0d.description: Senior Backend Engineer LiteLLM is the world’s most popular open-source AI Gateway, used by Adobe, Netflix, NASA, NVIDIA and much of the Fortune 500. Every LLM call these companies make runs through our code, so when we break, they break. We’re a team of about 20, and we’re hiring senior and staff backend engineers to own the core of the gateway and keep it fast and reliable as traffic grows. About the role You’ll own critical parts of the LiteLLM proxy: routing, auth, caching, spend tracking, guardrails and observability. The job is to make these systems correct, fast and dependable at 1B+ requests a month. That means hunting down silent failures, fixing the root cause in code rather than adding another dashboard, and refactoring components that keep breaking without changing how they behave. You’ll set the bar for how our mostly early-career team writes, tests and ships backend code. What you’ll do - Own core proxy components end to end, from design through production, including the incidents - Find and remove whole classes of bugs, like race conditions, stale cache state across replicas, and errors that get silently swallowed instead of shown to users - Make sure every guardrail and policy check (e.g. apply_guardrail) is logged, traceable and fails loudly when it should - Build guardrails that run inside the gateway and block common attacks on LLM APIs, MCP servers and agents - Keep our observability integrations (Datadog, Splunk, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry) accurate at 1B+ requests a month, with minimal latency overhead and no memory leaks (e.g. from Prometheus metric cardinality) - Help migrate performance-critical paths from Python to Rust without breaking behavior - Raise the bar for the team on code review, testing and debugging What we’re looking for - 2+ years building backend systems in production, with real ownership of something mission-critical: payments, gateways, core APIs, data stores, or anything else where downtime hurts customers - Strong Python, and experience with async or high-throughput services (asyncio, FastAPI or similar) - A track record of making production systems more reliable through code: refactors, re-architectures, migrations, or fixing a root cause for good - An excellent debugger across services, databases (Postgres, Redis) and distributed systems - High ownership, meaning you take responsibility for the customer impact of what you ship - BS/MS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent proof you’re exceptional Nice to have - Rust, Go or C++ in production - Time at a fast-growing startup with a large, real codebase - Experience with LLM APIs, proxies or API gateways - Open-source contributions Why LiteLLM - Your code runs in the critical path for some of the biggest companies in the world - Real ownership of core systems on a small, senior-leaning team - Profitable, growing fast, backed by Kleiner Perkins - $220-$260k base + equity, health, dental and vision. Onsite in San Francisco. About LiteLLM Li

We are growing our company with people who put team and mission first, value connection through laughter and joy, and work with humility and openness. We are committed to building a diverse, passionate, and creative team dedicated to a future powered by abundant, clean, low-cost energy.

 
 
Position Summary

 

The EHS Design and Engineering Integration Lead will embed EHS&S into Antora’s product design, equipment engineering, New Product Introduction (NPI), and manufacturing development processes. This role builds safety into existing engineering workflows, including design reviews, equipment specification, NPI gates, and change management. The role owns Antora’s Prevention through Design program and partners with NPI on the design of Antora’s upcoming factory. The role will apply first-principles thinking and Human and Organizational Performance (HOP) to build safety ownership within the teams it supports.

 

Who you are:  You are a safety engineer who believes EHS works best when it’s part of how engineering designs, builds, and changes things. You’ve worked inside design, equipment, and manufacturing engineering teams. You know how to turn hazard analysis into design criteria engineers use, so hazards get removed during design. You’re as comfortable facilitating a machine risk assessment or marking up an equipment layout as you are walking the site to see whether the work matches the plan. 

You’d rather set up an engagement model, standard, or tool that teams can use on their own. You size the program to Antora’s hazards and scale. You see design integration as part of Antora’s mission to stop global warming: the safer and more manufacturable our thermal energy storage systems are, the faster we can scale. You’re willing to grow your skillset as we build out our facilities and our upcoming factories. 

 

 

Roles & Responsibilities

    • Serve as the primary EHS&S contact for design engineering, NPI engineering, manufacturing engineering, and quality engineering. Learn how each team works and bring EHS&S in earlier, when hazards are cheapest to resolve.
    • Partner with design and NPI engineers to assess the safety manufacturability of Antora’s products, identifying design features that create manufacturing, assembly, or service risk.

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

This role answers that.  You will own the reliability models that predict the field failure rate over a product’s lifetime, the warranty data layer the company treats as source of truth, and the cross-functional programs that detect a problem in the field, contain it, and close it in collaboration with internal Engineering teams and the supplier.

Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We're looking for engineers to join Model-to-Product Behavior Engineering, the team responsible for getting Claude's behavior right across Anthropic's products. You'll work with product, research, and safeguards teams to make sure Claude behaves in ways that are consistent, safe, and genuinely helpful, whether in a new feature, a new model, or a launch.

Evals are one of the sharpest tools we have for getting Claude's behavior right, but not the only one. You'll build evals to see clearly where Claude shines and where it slips, use what you learn to inform how to close the gap, and build the harness improvements that get us there. That takes your own intuition and judgment about model behavior, both to decide what is worth building and to know what to do with what you find. Your work will shape launch decisions and give research and product teams a signal they can trust.

You'll also build the infrastructure behind our evals, along with tooling that makes it easy to test and ship prompt fixes. And you'll create self-serve tools that let other teams build their own evals and improve Claude's behavior in their products, so that getting model behavior right scales well beyond any one team.

You'll work across many projects and product surfaces at once, holding a high bar for the details while adapting as model capabilities change.

Key responsibilities

  • Build evals that measure Claude's quality, behavior, and capabilities across Anthropic's products and model releases, with sound methodology: deciding what to measure, validating datasets and graders, and interpreting noisy results with statistical rigor

  • Apply judgment to model outputs to separate real regressions and capability gaps from noise, and turn findings into clear recommendations

It's the isolated execution layer behind Perplexity Computer, the public Sandbox API, and a growing set of agent products. Every time an agent writes code, runs a tool, opens a browser, builds an app, or works on a user's files, it runs inside a SPACE sandbox. Two billion people around the world are actively trying to learn a language, but the best way to learn (one-on-one tutoring) is hard to access at scale and hasn’t been meaningfully improved in decades. Speak is building a human-level, AI-powered tutor in your pocket: a conversation-first experience that lets learners actually speak, get instant feedback, and progress through carefully designed lessons. The result is a complete path from beginner to confident speaker across multiple languages. Speak first launched in South Korea in 2019, where Speak has now become the number one language learning app, and we now serve learners across many markets and 15+ languages. Speak is one of the world’s leading AI companies, with over $150m raised in venture investment from OpenAI, Accel, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, and more, with a distributed team across San Francisco, Seoul, Tokyo, Taipei, and Ljubljana. ABOUT THIS ROLE We're looking for an engineer to join Speak's Infra Platform team at a pivotal moment: software development is undergoing a fundamental shift toward agentic workflows, and we're embracing it. Your team's mission is to help every engineering team at Speak own and operate its infrastructure. You'll provide reliable foundations, self-serve tooling, sensible guardrails, and hands-on guidance so teams can ship high-quality features quickly while delivering a state-of-the-art customer experience. The scope is broad and consequential: you'll drive velocity, reliability, and performance across our client apps, web, API, and infrastructure, while improving developer productivity. When Speak is fast and stable for millions of learners—and engineers can ship without friction—that's your team's impact. You'll also help lead Speak's agentic engineering transformation: moving beyond using AI to code faster and toward designing the systems, environments, and feedback loops that enable agents to work with increasing autonomy and quality. Platform is where that leverage compounds. The tools, environments, and guardrails you build will shape how effectively agents can work across the organization. We believe this shift is widening the gap between teams that fully embrace it and those that don't, and we're building for the former. We're looking for engineers who are excited to use coding agents to build faster, stay deep in the details, and lead by example. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING - Designing, building, and shipping the platform and infrastructure that other engineering teams rely on, using coding agents to move faster than was previously possible - Driving velocity and reliability across client apps, web, API, and infrastructure, and setting a high quality bar through your own work and your reviews - Leading the agentic engineering transformation from the front: constantly asking

You'll do that alongside our other Staff and Principal engineers, where direction gets set collectively rather than handed down. The experiences you'll own are defined by live sports. Increasingly the work is also realtime data: live stats, scores, and rankings arriving during a match and rendering correctly across every platform at once. This is a hands-on individual contributor role across iOS, Android, and our native TV platforms (Apple TV, Fire TV/Android TV). Our streaming footprint also includes Roku, Samsung, LG, and Vizio. 888132becd4c.description: Get to Know Us Horizon3 is a fast-growing, remote cybersecurity company dedicated to the mission of enabling organizations to proactively find and fix and verify exploitable attack vectors before criminals exploit them. Our flagship product, the NodeZeroTM platform, delivers production-safe autonomous pentests and other key assessment operations that scale across the largest internal, external, cloud, and hybrid cloud environments. We are a fusion of former U.S. Special Operations cyber operators, startup engineers, and formerly frustrated cybersecurity practitioners. We're committed to helping solve our common security problems: ineffective security tools, false positives resulting in alert fatigue, blind spots, "checkbox” security culture, cybersecurity skills shortage, and the long lead time and expense of hiring outside consultants. Collectively, we are a team of learn it alls, committed to a culture of respect, collaboration, ownership, and results. An Overview We're looking for a Senior AI Engineer to build the intelligence that makes NodeZero's external attack capabilities go beyond deterministic attacks and locate advanced breach vectors. You'll use AI agent frameworks and reasoning systems that transform fragmented external data into actionable intelligence. That means connecting assets, identities, exposed credentials, infrastructure, and code repositories into a coherent understanding of an organization's external attack surface. You'll develop systems that reason over incomplete information, investigate hypotheses, determine what matters, and intelligently leverage existing offensive capabilities and go beyond them. The hard part isn't collecting more data or automating another attack technique. It's building AI that can reason through the ambiguity of real-world environments. An exposed credential might connect to an overlooked application, a Git repository might reveal an unexpected trust relationship, and an apparently unrelated domain might provide the missing context for an attack path. Traditional automation struggles with the complexity, uncertainty, and long tail of these relationships. You'll combine agentic architectures, retrieval, graph-based reasoning, and deterministic tools to build systems that can navigate these problems at scale. Success here isn’t judged by how plausible an answer reads. It’s judged by outcomes: did the agent surface an asset, credential, or attack path our deterministic tools missed, and did it validate it? You’ll build the evaluation frameworks, feedback loops, and production infrastructure that make these systems increasingly capable and reliable. And because they operate in real customer environments, you'll ensure their reasoning and actions remain safe, explainable, and strict

About the Company

We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.

The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries.

About the Job

Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean’s harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention.

As a Computational Engineer, you will work with our in-house Python automation tools to run computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations from geometry to report: meshing, case setup, solving on HPC systems, and post-processing. Our fast-running reduced-order models (ROMs) are used to explore and optimize marine system designs, and the CFD automation tools are how we check their predictions against high-fidelity simulation. Your job will be to make that check faster, more reliable, and easier to trust.

You will work in Python every day: running verification cases, finding out why a simulation failed or a result looks wrong, and turning what you learn into better defaults, templates, and automated checks. You will implement the team’s CFD best practices in the workflow so that every run follows them without extra manual effort. You will also improve how CFD and ROM results are compared, so that agreement and disagreement are measured consistently and reported clearly. You will work closely with senior CFD engineers, who will set technical direction, review your work, and help with the hardest problems. You will also have cross-team collaborations with the engineers who develop the ROMs.

This is an early-career role. The ideal candidate has a solid foundation in fluid mechanics, hands-on CFD experience from coursework, research, internships, or industry, and a strong interest in scripting and automation. We are looking for someone who is careful with details, curious about why a simulation gives the answer it does, and motivated to write code that removes manual steps.

We turn these moments into signals that help Physical AI labs and robotics teams understand which failures their data covers, where it falls short, and what belongs in their next training run. We’ve raised $30M from investors like Felicis, CRV, Y Combinator, and angels from the co-founders of Databricks and Perplexity. Our team comes from AWS, Lyft, and Tesla. 8cf691abcd67.description: At Expedia Group, we help travelers explore the world, one journey at a time. As a global travel company powered by passionate people, trusted partnerships, and leading technology, we connect travelers, partners, and advertisers through our consumer brands, B2B network, and travel advertising business. Here, you'll do meaningful work that helps millions of people discover, book, and experience travel with more ease, confidence, and joy. Our five Behaviors-Traveler First, Think Big, Operate with Excellence, Ownership Mindset, and Succeed Together-help foster a supportive environment where people can grow their careers and have the flexibility, benefits, and support to do their best work. Join us and build for travelers everywhere. Please note that this role is only available in Chicago, IL . Introduction to the Team Expedia Group Advertising helps Expedia Group and its partners connect with travelers and understand the impact of advertising across Expedia Group brands and partner channels. Within Emerging Business Technology, the Measurement, Attribution & Data Platform organization builds the data, measurement, and attribution capabilities that translate advertising interactions and outcomes into trusted insights. As a Data Scientist III, you will shape how we measure advertising performance and outcomes. You’ll apply statistical methods, causal inference, experimentation, and predictive modeling to complex, large-scale datasets—developing approaches that help distinguish the impact of advertising from other factors in a traveler’s journey. Your work will inform attribution, measurement, and reporting experiences used by advertisers and internal teams to make better decisions. You’ll partner closely with engineering, product, and analytics stakeholders to define measurement problems, evaluate data quality and assumptions, and turn analytical methods into scalable, reliable solutions. You’ll bring scientific rigor to ambiguous questions, communicate findings and tradeoffs clearly, and help ensure that insights are actionable and trustworthy in production. We’re looking for a data scientist who takes ownership of high-impact work, exercises sound judgment, and raises the bar for analytical quality. At this level, you’ll lead projects from problem framing through validation and adoption, influence measurement strategy, and help evolve the platforms and methods Expedia Group uses to understand advertising outcomes. In This Role, You Will Analyze large, complex datasets to solve business and product challenges. Develop and apply statistical, machine learning, and experimentation methodologies to generate actionable insights. Build scalable analytical solutions, dashboards, and measurement frameworks. Communicate findings and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences. Mentor junior team members and contribute to analytics best practices. f9af8e6fabad.title: Design Engineer
f9af8e6fabad.description: ABOUT US Medical data exchange is one of the biggest unsolved problems in US healthcare. If you've spent any real time in the healthcare system, you've felt it, and it only gets worse the sicker and older you get. Metriport exists to fix that. We connect to the data sources the healthcare providers of tomorrow need, take raw data that's unusable in its source form, and turn it into a single clean format that care teams, and their agents, actually use to improve outcomes. Record retrieval across thousands of legacy systems and antiquated data pipes that used to take weeks now takes seconds. Clinicians walk into appointments with the full patient picture already in hand, and that speed can mean spotting a condition early enough to actually treat it. We're not a healthcare company. We're a technology company that happens to operate in healthcare, and we build every layer ourselves: connect, transform, and insight. Legacy EHRs were built to get providers paid, not to serve the clinical experience. We're building what should have existed instead: the system of record for all of US healthcare. We started in data exchange. Today we compete with the largest data platforms in the space. Tomorrow we will be the infrastructure layer healthcare runs on. We’ve raised $28.4 million from top tier VCs (including Matrix, ARTIS and Y Combinator), found product market fit (multi million dollar ARR, 100+ customers including Amazon One Medical, Circle Medical, Color Health, and Strive Health), and have years of runway ahead of us. If you’ve had a good healthcare experience in the past few years, there’s a good chance Metriport was behind it. That’s the version of healthcare we want people to not just expect, but demand. Join us and build the future. About You We're a small, high output team, mostly former founders including YC alumni, and we operate with real autonomy and almost no bureaucracy. We hire on competence, not pedigree. Leaders are in the office six days a week, not because we count hours, but because there's always more wood to chop when revolutionizing how tomorrow’s healthcare providers deliver care to their patients today. We trust our team to take the time off they need and we've never said no to a time off request. You have an entrepreneurial mindset and a strong sense of ownership. You don't wait to be told what's broken. Instead, you believe you can figure out any problem that lands in your lap even outside your exact domain. When someone scopes something for three weeks, you ask why it can't be done in three days, and you also know the difference between shipping a fast v0 and cutting a corner that comes back to bite you. You walk the tightrope between craft and speed without falling off either side. df5edc1ceab8.description:
Why AssemblyAI

AssemblyAI builds the best-in-class Voice AI models powering the next generation of voice applications. We have a lab, and we also power our own models in our own proprietary inference environment. Our models serve 500M+ inference calls monthly, and process nearly 2 million hours of audio daily. The Voice AI space is at an inflection point; we’re looking for the best talent we can find to join a rapidly scaling team that's defining the future of the industry.

We are one of the most capital-efficient AI companies on the planet - and are rapidly approaching $1M ARR per employee. We sit among the top 5 most revenue-dense teams within the fastest-growing AI companies today. We have thousands of customers building with us including the top startups and world-renowned enterprises, and are serving at tremendous scale: we process nearly 2 million hours of audio daily and handle more than 15 million API calls every day. This is a rare growth-stage opportunity where the business is proven, the revenue is durable, and the growth trajectory is steep and getting steeper. We have a super flat culture and expect our employees to be deeply intimate with the details at all levels.

If you've ever felt buried under layers of bureaucracy, starved of real ownership, or frustrated watching your work disappear into a slow-moving org, AssemblyAI is built differently. The company operates as a true meritocracy, with no heavy planning or approval processes and no gatekeeping on the tools or information you need. For anyone who genuinely cares about voice AI, not as a trend to chase, but as a technology to build, this is the place where the most interesting problems at the most interesting scale are being solved by a team small enough that you'll actually know everyone's name.

About the role:

AssemblyAI is hiring a Senior Analytics Engineer to build the agents that do analytics engineering work, and to help run the data infrastructure they work in.

Our Analytics team owns a broad and expanding set of data domains—including revenue, ARR, product usage, cost, go-to-market metrics, and customer behavior—with new domains added as product launches dictate. Every team at AssemblyAI relies on our centralized warehouse, dbt projects, and semantic layer for single-source-of-truth reporting.

You will own some of these domains outright. Which ones depends on your strengths and where the team needs you, and the mix will change as the company grows. You will also know the others well enough to review a teammate’s changes and cover for them when needed.

We already lean on agents across the team, and want them to do most of the routine work of an analytics or data engineer. You will build the environment that makes that possible. That means agents that write and review dbt models, add tests and documentation, triage failed runs, trace a wron

Our roster has an opening with your name on it
